blocks.text: VPN access policy rules enable you to allow or block network traffic on VPN Service Edges. VPN (for Legacy Apps) supports a maximum of 1,000 policy rules. For a complete list of ranges and limitations for access policy rules, see Ranges & Limitations.

Per Private Access (ZPA) policy evaluation, VPN (for Legacy Apps) evaluates access policy rules using a top-down, specific-match principle. Traffic that doesn't match any access policy rule is blocked by default. If you are new to VPN (for Legacy Apps), you must create a policy rule to allow any traffic through the VPN tunnel.

Before you configure an access policy rule, consider configuring IP address objects for grouping Classless Inter-Domain Routings (CIDRs) and IP addresses that can be used as a source or destination network in multiple policy rules to help organize the network resources to protect.
To configure an access policy rule:

blocks.item: Go to Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Access Policy.
Click Add Rule.
The Add Rule page appears.
On the Add Rule page:
Source Networks: Select an option to define the source:

IP Addresses: Select and enter an IP address, and click Add. A maximum of 64 IP addresses or IP subnets is allowed. You can also click Import LAN/Client Subnets or Address Book to define sources from a predefined list.
IdP Attributes: Select identity providers to create access rules and choose one of the following:

​​​​​​​Add SAML Attributes: Click Any SAML Attribute if you want to allow logs for any user to be streamed (i.e., the policy applies to any users, groups, departments, etc.). By default, the policy is set to Any SAML attribute from an IdP. Click a specific SAML attribute if you want to allow logs for only specific users, groups, departments, etc. to be streamed. You can also search for a specific group. After you make a selection, enter the SAML attribute value (i.e., the users to whom the policy applies) in the text field that appears. Click More SAML Attributes to add multiple attributes, if necessary.

Add SCIM Attributes: From the drop-down menu, select the SCIM attribute you want to be streamed. You can also search for a specific SCIM attribute. After you select the SCIM attribute, select the SCIM user. Click More SCIM Attributes to add multiple SCIM attributes, if necessary.

Add SCIM Group Attributes: From the drop-down menu, select the SCIM group you want to be streamed. You can also search for a specific SCIM group. Click More SCIM Group Attributes to add multiple SCIM groups, if necessary.
Click Import IdP Attribute Object to apply a preconfigured set of IdP criteria.
Destination Networks: Select an option to define the destination:

IP Addresses: Select and enter an IP address, and click Add. A maximum of 64 IP addresses or IP subnets is allowed. You can also click Import LAN/Client Subnets or Address Book to define destinations from a predefined list.
IdP Attributes: Select identity providers to create access rules and choose one of the following:

Add SAML Attributes: Click Any SAML Attribute if you want to allow logs for any user to be streamed (i.e., the policy applies to any users, groups, departments, etc.). By default, the policy is set to Any SAML attribute from an IdP. Click a specific SAML attribute if you want to allow logs for only specific users, groups, departments, etc. to be streamed. You can also search for a specific group. After you make a selection, enter the SAML attribute value (i.e., the users to whom the policy applies) in the text field that appears. Click More SAML Attributes to add multiple attributes, if necessary.

Add SCIM Attributes: From the drop-down menu, select the SCIM attribute you want to be streamed. You can also search for a specific SCIM attribute. After you select the SCIM attribute, select the SCIM user. Click More SCIM Attributes to add multiple SCIM attributes, if necessary.

Add SCIM Group Attributes: From the drop-down menu, select the SCIM group you want to be streamed. You can also search for a specific SCIM group. Click More SCIM Group Attributes to add multiple SCIM groups, if necessary.
Click Import IdP Attribute Object to apply a preconfigured set of IdP criteria.
Protocols: Select an IP protocol for communication.
Action: Select one of the following actions when the traffic matches the rule:
Allow: Allows access to the network.
Block: Blocks access to the network.
Rule Name: Enter a name for the access policy rule. The name cannot contain special characters, except for periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Rule Status: Select Enabled or Disabled to activate or deactivate the rule.
See image.
Click Save.
